The Exile cannot win as Usurper in the same Act. At their next Wake, they first check for victory while still Oathkeeper; then, if still holding title, flip it to Usurper. Their first Usurper win check is the following Wake, unless round 8 ends first while they remain Usurper. Losing the title prevents the win; retaking it resets the title to Oathkeeper and restarts the sequence.

given_state: An Exile takes the Oathkeeper title during their Act.
completed_events: The title transfer has happened during Act; that turn’s Wake is already over.
next_operation: At the Exile’s next Wake check victory, then flip to Usurper if still titleholder.
result: First ordinary Usurper victory check is the following Wake; loss of title prevents it, and retaking resets the sequence.

The Oaths and matching true Visions are Supremacy—Conquest (rule the most sites); People—Rebellion (hold People’s Favor); Protection—Sanctuary (hold the most relics and banners); Devotion—Faith (hold Darkest Secret). A Visionary win also requires the Exile to have the true Vision revealed, complete its goal at Wake, and at least 3 world-deck Visions drawn by all players combined. For Conquest and Sanctuary, “most” means strictly more than every other player; a tie does not count.
Oathkeeper title and four Oaths|Visionary victory

Roll the end die at the end of rounds 5, 6, and 7 only if the Chancellor or a Citizen is Oathkeeper. The game ends on 6 in round 5, 5–6 in round 6, or 3–6 in round 7. An Exile Oathkeeper/Usurper prevents the roll.

At the end of round 8, resolve in order: (1) if Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper, Empire wins; a qualified Citizen Successor wins alone instead of Chancellor; (2) otherwise an Exile Usurper wins; (3) otherwise a qualifying revealed Exile Vision wins, with simultaneous qualifiers ordered Conquest, Rebellion, Sanctuary, Faith; (4) otherwise Empire wins, again with a qualified Successor replacing Chancellor. An Exile merely holding Oathkeeper does not stop the round-8 fallback.
War exhaustion|Citizen succession is a separate test|Visionary victory

Under Supremacy, a Citizen must hold more relics and banners combined than the Chancellor and every other Citizen. Under People, hold Darkest Secret; under Protection, hold People’s Favor; under Devotion, hold Grand Scepter. A Citizen cannot win through a true Vision or Usurper status. Successor status matters only when Chancellor would otherwise win; it never ends the game alone.
Citizen succession is a separate test

At Wake, if holding People’s Favor, choose to add 1 favor from your board or return 1 from it to a least-full suit bank (choose among tied banks). Never remove its last favor: at 1, add if able; if unable, do nothing. If already Mob-side, repeat the choice once. After these choices, flip it to Mob if it has 6 or more favor; becoming Mob at this last check does not add a retroactive choice.

Rest order: (1) return favor on denizens/edifices to matching suit banks; (2) return secrets on denizens/edifices/relics to your board and flip facedown board secrets faceup; (3) Exile/Chancellor refresh Supply to the space for warbands remaining in their personal bank (Chancellor: 18+→6, 11–17→5, 4–10→4, 0–3→3; Exile: 9+→6, 4–8→5, 0–3→4); Citizen refreshes to the Chancellor’s exact marker space. Then (4) save remaining unspent Supply by moving marker one extra space left per point, capped at leftmost/7 Supply; (5) optional Rest powers.

Search chooses either the world deck or the discard pile for your pawn’s region, never both. Discard Search costs 2 Supply. World Search costs 2 at 0 Visions drawn, 3 at 1–2, or 4 at 3–5; Darkest Secret makes world Search cost 2, with other modifiers still applying. Draw 3, fewer only if source runs out, a world Vision stops the draw, or a modifier reduces it; you cannot stop voluntarily. A world-deck Vision is announced, stops Search immediately, and advances the track by 1. A Vision drawn from discard neither stops the draw nor advances the track.

Hand/adviser discards go to the next region’s pile in the Cradle→Provinces→Hinterland→Cradle cycle, based on your pawn’s region, never the same-region pile. When discarding a card at a site in another region, use that card’s region for the cycle. Favor on discarded cards returns immediately to its matching bank; their secrets go facedown to the acting player’s board.

There may be up to 3 advisers total, counting faceup and facedown. Before exceeding the limit, discard an adviser if permitted; locks still apply. A facedown adviser has no suit, restriction, or power; any card, including site-only cards and Visions, may be held facedown. Later, a facedown adviser may be played faceup legally or discarded as a minor action; a faceup adviser cannot be discarded at will. A revealed true Vision goes in the Exile’s separate Revealed Vision space, not an adviser slot, and replaces/discards the previous revealed true Vision.
Search — 2–4 Supply|Adviser retention depends on its state

Muster costs 1 Supply: place 1 favor on an empty denizen or intact edifice at your pawn’s site, then gain 2 warbands from your personal bank to your board; Citizens gain purple. Relics and ruins are ineligible; you need not rule the site. Trade costs 1 Supply and uses an empty denizen/intact edifice at your pawn’s site: put 1 secret on it to gain 1 favor plus 1 per matching faceup adviser from its suit bank, or put 2 favor on it to gain 1 shared-bank secret per matching faceup adviser. Facedown advisers do not match; if none match, the second option gains zero secrets, but the cost remains payable. Finite sources limit gains.

Recover costs 1 Supply plus target cost. A facedown relic must be at your site; pay its printed site cost and hold it faceup in your personal bank. Either banner can be recovered from anywhere (including you or shared bank). For People’s Favor, pay strictly more favor than it currently has, add payment to it, distribute its old favor one at a time through suit banks starting at a chosen bank, then flip Mob to normal; no seizure penalty applies. For Darkest Secret, pay strictly more secrets than it has, place them on it, take 1 old secret and give the rest to prior holder (if yourself, all old secrets return to you; shared-bank remainder stays there).

Another player’s Darkest Secret is recoverable only if their pawn’s site has at least one suited card whose suit matches none of their faceup advisers; one mismatch suffices even if other cards match. Thus a site with no suited cards is safe, and a ruin-only site is safe (ruins have no suit). With no faceup advisers, any suited card at the site is unmatched and permits recovery. Self-recovery and recovery from shared bank ignore this protection.
Darkest Secret protection, corrected by official errata

Choose any other player who rules your site or has their pawn there as defender. If no player rules your site, bandits may be chosen. At least one target must be at your pawn’s site; if defender rules that site, you must target it. You may add any defender sites elsewhere on the map, one defense die each. If defender’s pawn is at your site, you may also target their relics, banners, or pawn and favor together; those co-located targets use their printed dice and a same-site relic itself satisfies the local-target requirement.

Attack dice: attacker chooses up to the number of warbands in the full attacking force; fewer dice do not remove unrolled warbands from that force. Defense dice are printed target dice plus mandatory title bonus and modifiers. Defense equals shields (each double symbol doubles shield results, multipliers stack) plus warbands at targeted sites, plus defender board force if their pawn is at attacker site or a target site; bandits add 1 per targeted bandit site. Doubles multiply shields only. Each attack skull kills one of attacker’s force warbands immediately. Full swords count one each; each pair of hollow swords adds one, leftover hollow sword zero. Attacker wins only by strictly exceeding defense. May sacrifice own surviving force warbands for +1 each, but if sacrificing, exactly enough to win, never excess.

On attacker victory, first the defender kills half its defending force, rounded down; then resolve defeated battle-plan effects. The attacker may place any number—including zero—of surviving force warbands at targeted sites. Taking zero leaves a site to bandits unless a power applies. Take all targeted relics and banners; banner seizure other than Recover burns 2 resources down to minimum 1 and flips People’s Favor to Mob. If pawn/favor was targeted, attacker may force defender to travel to a legal chosen destination for no Supply and independently may burn half defender’s board favor rounded down. Banishment gives the no-Supply permission; destination and entry restrictions still apply, subject to named overrides.

When an Imperial player defends, Chancellor automatically joins as Ally; other nonattacking Citizens may join with permission if their pawn is at attacker’s site or a target. Apply their relevant modifiers and share powers as one defending side, but “your site/board” still refers to each player’s own. Allied board warbands count only if pawn is at attacker site or target. The side may use plans at Imperial sites and own advisers, each shared plan once total by one user who pays; declared defender decides contested order/timing/priority. Chancellor chooses Imperial casualties; surviving site warbands return to Chancellor’s board, while surviving Citizen-board warbands remain there. In a Citizen attack on Chancellor or another Citizen, that attacker is temporarily non-Imperial; if Chancellor attacks a Citizen, that defender is temporarily non-Imperial.

Base Travel costs by origin→destination region: Cradle 1/2/4 to Cradle/Provinces/Hinterland; Provinces 2/2/2; Hinterland 4/2/3. Travel to a different site, reveal it if facedown, put its printed favor/secrets there from shared bank, and place its printed relic count facedown beside it from relic deck. Apply fixed-number cost first, then increases/decreases; a final applicable “spend no Supply” power makes payment zero. Entry restrictions remain unless ignored.

The Grand Scepter holder may offer any Exile, including themself, Citizenship on a later turn—not the turn they took the Scepter—and must promise exactly one Reliquary relic. They may negotiate a binding exchange of favor, secrets, banners, and non-Reliquary relics; Reliquary relics cannot be traded by other binding-deal powers. Acceptance flips recipient to Citizen, replaces their board/map warbands with purple (recipient chooses removals if supply is short), discards revealed Vision, flips Usurper to Oathkeeper, ends their Act if it is their turn, and refreshes to full Supply. Exchange promised pieces; Chancellor gains the newly uncovered mandatory Reliquary modifier.

Chronicle: if victory was by Vision alone, next Oath matches that Vision; for any other or multiple victory methods, choose any Oath except the current one. If an Exile wins, flip all Citizen boards (even boxed) to Exile, then may offer Chronicle Citizenship to other Exiles except those just flipped; acceptors become Citizens and replace every garrison at each site they rule with exactly one winner-color warband. To rebuild: shuffle remaining in-play denizens; top 10 denizens + 2 random Visions (12); next 15 denizens + remaining 3 Visions (18); rest denizens below. The Chronicle aid’s “12 denizens + 2” is an error, so top stack is 12 cards, not 14.
